exams.title: Medical Billing Fundamentals & ERA/EOB Posting
exams.description: Initial benchmark evaluation covering deductibles (PR 1), ERA eligible payment methods, payer networks, EOB workflows, and CO 253 sequestration adjustments.

questions.text: What is Deductible (PR 1)?
options: A copay charged per specialist consultation
The specific out-of-pocket amount a patient must pay annually before health insurance begins to cover costs
A flat administrative charge deducted by the hospital
A penalty applied for out-of-network claims

questions.text: Which payment methods are eligible for ERA posting?
options: Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT / ACH) and Non-payment postings

questions.text: Name at least four payer networks mentioned in the training document.
options: Cigna International, Bupa, Allianz, AXA only

questions.text: Who sends an EOB, and what information does it provide?
options: Sent by the patient to summarize symptoms
Sent by the payer/insurance company to the provider explaining how the claim was processed (allowed amounts, adjustments, patient responsibility)
Sent by the court to mandate collection actions
Sent by the credentialing team to verify addresses

questions.text: What is a patient statement?
options: A medical diagnosis summary for insurance pre-authorization
A financial communication document sent to the patient summarizing account activity and outstanding balance

questions.text: Why should the billing address be reviewed before posting an ERA?
options: To verify the patient home zip code
To ensure the ERA payment is posted to the correct provider account and avoid payment disruptions/misallocation
To calculate sales tax for medical services

questions.text: What are the methods a patient statement can be generated?
options: Paper-based statement and Electronic statement (e.g. via PMS / Healow portal)

questions.text: What is Claim Adjustment Reason Code CO 253 (Sequestration)?
options: Sequestration — Mandatory Federal budget reduction for Medicare and managed care plans

questions.text: How will a Virtual Credit Card (VCC) payment be processed?
options: Post directly into the PMS as an EFT transaction without verification
VCCs should not be posted as-is; contact the payer via phone to request reissuance as Paper Check or EFT
Deposit immediately into employee petty cash
Decline the claim and write off the balance

questions.text: What is the purpose of the weekly payment report?
options: To monitor each client average target, predict cash flow trends, catch weekly lows, and meet monthly financial goals
To file state tax returns every week

exams.title: RCM Advanced Workflow, Patient Responsibility & Turnaround Time
exams.description: Comprehensive 15-question evaluation on Patient Responsibility, ERA address mismatches, Virtual Cards, Contract Rates, Statement Cycles, TAT (48h), and CO 144.

questions.text: 1. What is meant by patient responsibility in the statement process?
options: The specific out-of-pocket amount a patient must pay after insurance processes and adjudicates a claim

questions.text: 2. The billing address on an ERA does not match the practice's registered address. What are the next steps?
options: Ignore the mismatch and post immediately
Notify the credentialing team via email to contact the payer and update the address
Send the bill to the patient

questions.text: 3. A payer sends a virtual credit card payment. What action must be taken before posting?
options: Contact the payer to request reissuance as EFT or Paper Check

questions.text: 4. What is the purpose of verifying the payer network/rate before posting?
options: To ensure the allowed amount matches the payer contracted rate and prevent provider revenue loss
To confirm patient insurance card color

questions.text: 5. What is the purpose of monitoring the number of statements sent to a patient?
options: To ensure statements follow standard protocol (up to 3 cycles) before moving accounts to DSEND or collections

questions.text: 6. Why is it important to process EOBs within the expected turnaround time?
options: To maintain healthy practice cash flow, prevent revenue loss, and address claim denials promptly
To close monthly fiscal years early

questions.text: 7. What is the required TAT for processing an EOB after it has been scanned into the system?
options: 24 to 48 hours from the date scanned into the PMS

questions.text: 8. Why is it important to send patient statements promptly?
options: To ensure timely patient payment collections, sustain cash flow, and minimize aging Accounts Receivable

questions.text: 9. What is the purpose of sending a patient statement?
options: To advertise new medical clinic services
To provide clear financial communication of the remaining account balance after insurance adjudication

questions.text: 10. Why might an insurance payer take an offset from a current payment?
options: To recover an overpayment made on a previous claim identified during insurance audits
To pay for medical records courier fees

questions.text: 11. Why should patient balances be reviewed before generating statements?
options: To ensure patients have good credit
To verify recent PMS payments, prevent duplicate statements, and eliminate billing mistakes

questions.text: 12. If the patient still does not pay after subsequent statements, what can be done?
options: Discharge patient from medical care immediately
Transfer the account to Collections Agency or DSEND status based on provider protocol

questions.text: 13. Based on which policy can a patient account be submitted to collections or DSEND?
options: Provider and Client financial/statement cycle policy after 3 uncollected statements

questions.text: 14. What is the client promise made by ABC (Apple Billing & Credentialing)?
options: To process all ERA and scanned EOBs within 48 hours Turnaround Time with high quality

questions.text: 15. What is Claim Adjustment Code CO 144?
options: Incentive Adjustment — Positive MIPS incentive adjustment for Medicare and managed care plans based on provider quality

exams.title: Claim Submission Fundamentals — 1st Assessment
exams.description: 10-question foundational assessment covering claim submission concepts, clearinghouse roles, batch management, payer IDs, and rejection types.

questions.text: 1. What is claim submission?
options: The process of submitting claims electronically or manually to insurance payers for proper reimbursement

questions.text: 2. Why are claims submitted twice a day?
options: To ensure all claims are submitted on time, avoid missing claims, reduce delays, and receive timely reimbursement

questions.text: 3. What is the consequence of not submitting a claim?
options: The claim may be delayed, rejected, denied or result in timely filing issues causing revenue loss

questions.text: 4. Write the types of claim submission.
options: Electronic (EDI/clearinghouse), Online payer portal, and Manual (paper/fax) submission

questions.text: 5. In electronic claim submission, claims are transmitted through:
6. What is the role of a clearinghouse?
options: To review claims for errors, validate information, and transmit claims to the appropriate payer to reduce rejections and speed reimbursement

questions.text: 7. Manual claim submission uses which form?
8. What is manual claim submission?
options: Submitting paper CMS-1500 or UB-04 claim forms directly to the payer via mail or fax

questions.text: 9. What is online payer portal submission?
options: Submitting claims via a third-party agency
Submitting claims directly through a payer's secure web portal without a clearinghouse

questions.text: 10. Which claim submission team task involves reviewing claims with system issues?

exams.title: Claim Submission Advanced — Final Assessment
exams.description: 15-question comprehensive assessment on Payer IDs, clearinghouse workflow, batch management, rejection handling, HCFA printing, and why claim submission drives revenue.

questions.text: 1. How many times should claims be submitted each day?
options: Twice a day (1 PM and 4 PM) to ensure timely reimbursement and avoid missed batches

questions.text: 2. Which information is included in a claim?
options: Patient name, Member ID, DOS, DX/CPT codes, Insurance, Rendering Provider, Facility, Billed amount

questions.text: 3. What is a Payer ID?
options: A unique 5-digit numeric or alphanumeric identifier assigned to an insurance payer for electronic claim routing

questions.text: 4. Payer ID is mainly required for:
options: Submitting the claim electronically through a clearinghouse to route it to the correct payer

questions.text: 5. What is the purpose of a clearinghouse?
options: To review claims for errors, validate information, transmit to the correct payer, reduce rejections, and speed reimbursement

questions.text: 6. What is a claim batch?
options: A collection of multiple healthcare claims grouped together and submitted as a single electronic file for processing

questions.text: 7. If a batch is missing, what should we do?
options: Check the clearinghouse portal; if the batch is not found after the cutoff time, resubmit the batch

questions.text: 8. If Payer ID is missing, what will happen?
options: The claim cannot be submitted electronically; it must be submitted via alternative methods or the payer ID must be found first
The clearinghouse assigns a default ID

questions.text: 9. What is rejection and the types of rejection?
options: Rejection occurs when a clearinghouse or payer refuses to process a claim due to errors or missing info. Types: 1. Clearinghouse Rejection 2. Insurance Rejection

questions.text: 10. Why does insurance request medical records?
options: To verify the patient's information, ensure medical necessity, and confirm the services billed before issuing payment

questions.text: 11. Why are we adding Modifier 25 for E&M services?
options: When E&M services and another procedure are billed on the same day, Modifier 25 indicates the E&M was a separately identifiable service
Because the payer requires it for all claims

questions.text: 12. What is the correct general sequence for rejection handling?
13. Why are we doing Print HCFA?
options: When electronic or payer portal submission is not supported, the CMS-1500 (HCFA) paper claim form is printed and faxed or mailed to the payer

questions.text: 14. Which task should we prioritize first: faxing or printing the HCFA forms?
options: Faxing first — it is faster and gets the document directly to the insurance company, reducing payment delays

questions.text: 15. Why is claim submission important?
options: Claim submission is the primary mechanism for providers to receive payment from insurers. Without it, there is no revenue.

submissions.examTitle: RCM Advanced Workflow, Patient Responsibility & Turnaround Time

answersDetail.1. Patient Responsibility: Patient responsibility means the specific amount a patient must pay from out of pocket, after insurance company processes and adjudicates a claim. It can be copay or coinsurance
answersDetail.2. Address Mismatch: If the billing address does not match the practice registered address, we need to update the current address. To update the address we must inform the credentialing team via Email.
answersDetail.3. Virtual Credit Card: Most common payment method is EFT and Paper check. Virtual credit card payment is difficult to process so we reissue the card payment to EFT or paper checks
answersDetail.4. Verify Payer Network Rate: Purpose of verifying payer network rate is to avoid payment loss. For example if payer allowed amount is $350 but we fix the billed amount as $200, there is a payment loss of $100.
answersDetail.5. Statement Monitoring: For each statement there is a certain amount provider needs to pay. We send maximum three statements after that it moves to DSEND status or collection policy.
answersDetail.6. EOB Turnaround Time: Processing Explanation of Benefits within the expected turnaround time is to maintain good cash flow and manage denials.
answersDetail.7. Required TAT: Turnaround Time for processing and posting a scanned EOB into a practice management system is 24 to 48 hours.
answersDetail.8. Prompt Patient Statements: Sending patient statements promptly for good cash flow and ensuring patients pay the amount on time.
answersDetail.9. Purpose of Statement: Patient statement is a financial communication explaining the balance amount which should be paid by the patient. The primary purpose is to clearly communicate a patient's financial responsibility after insurance processing.
answersDetail.10. Payer Offset / Overpayment: Insurance payer takes an offset from current payment because of overpayment of the previous claim. Insurance audits every year; if they find any overpayment they deduct the remaining amount from future claims.
answersDetail.11. Balance Review before Statement: Patient may pay the amount directly to the practice which is then scanned in PMS so we must check the PMS before sending statements
answersDetail.12. Delinquent Patient Accounts: If a patient payment remains unpaid after sending three statements it moves to DSEND or Collection status. Healow helps to send statements electronically.
answersDetail.13. Collections Policy: Healow helps to submit statements electronically.
answersDetail.14. ABC Client Promise: ABC commits to processing ERA and EOBs within the turnaround time which is 48 hours. The ERA and EOB must be processed from the date they are scanned.
answersDetail.15. CO 144: CO-144 — Incentive Adjustment — It is a positive adjustment made by MIPS for Medicare and managed care plans. It is based on the quality of service provided by the provider.

submissions.examTitle: RCM Advanced Workflow, Patient Responsibility & Turnaround Time

answersDetail.1. Patient Responsibility: The Patient Responsibility is the amount paid by the patient from his own pocket. Hence we are sending the Statement to the Patient.
answersDetail.2. Address Mismatch: The Registered address was not a match, then we send an email to the Credentialing team to inform the payer to correct the address in the ERA and reissue it.
answersDetail.3. Virtual Credit Card: The virtual card is sent by the payer; we are not to post the cashing details without client approval. We check and call the payer to inform that the payment will be processed as an EFT Format.
answersDetail.4. Verify Payer Network Rate: The purpose to check the payer network rate is to cross-check that the allowed amount is correctly posted on the claim for every line item.
answersDetail.5. Statement Monitoring: The patient statements also have a particular rate — every patient receives only 3 statements.
answersDetail.6. EOB Turnaround Time: We process the EOB within the particular time so the payment will be received by the provider on a correct schedule.
answersDetail.7. Required TAT: The turnaround time for EOB processing will be on the same day.

answersDetail.9. Purpose of Statement: The purpose of sending a statement to the patient is to get the payment paid from the patient side and send it to the provider.
answersDetail.10. Payer Offset / Overpayment: An offset is when a payer mistakenly provides excess payment to that particular claim — for the same patient the next claim the payer will not provide that payment again.
answersDetail.11. Balance Review before Statement: The patient statement is only provided when the patient responsibility amount is due; we check the patient balance before generating the statement.
answersDetail.12. Delinquent Patient Accounts: We provide 3 statements to the patient and if they do not respond then we give the claim to a collection agency to follow and get the patient balance amount.
answersDetail.13. Collections Policy: Based on TAT policy: if the patient does not respond to the actions taken then we handover the claim to collections agency or DSEND — the DSEND process is concluded by the providers approval.
answersDetail.14. ABC Client Promise: We make the actions to get the payment in the claim within 48 hours.
answersDetail.15. CO 144: The CO 144 is a penalty for the provider if services are not enough for the patient — then only the penalty is concluded for the provider.

answersDetail.8. If Payer ID is Missing, what will hap: Check the clearinghouse first; the claim was not submitted, manually post the claim.
answersDetail.10. Why insurance requesting medical rec: Ensure the medical record is verified after the payment is received; accurate and supported by documentation
answersDetail.11. Why we are adding modifier 25 for E&: Modifier 25 is used when an E/M service is separately identified from another procedure done on the same day.
answersDetail.13. Why we are doing Print HCFA?: Verify the address, then check the HUB, demographic face sheet, and facility information. After confirmation, send the printed HCFA
answersDetail.14. Which task should we prioritize firs: The first to prioritize is fax
answersDetail.15. Why claim submission is important?: Submitting the claims is important because if we don't submit regularly, it may cause delay to get payment and reduce overflow in the overall process.

answersDetail.1. How many times should claims be submi: Claims have been submitted twice a day.
answersDetail.2. Which information is included in a cl: Provider name, location, DOS, CPT, Diagnosis, Insurance
answersDetail.3. What is a Payer ID?: Payer ID is a unique 5 digit numeric or alphanumeric number for an insurance payer.
answersDetail.4. Payer ID is mainly required for:: Payer ID is mainly required for submitting claim electronically through clearinghouse.
answersDetail.5. Purpose of clearing house: Clearing house purpose is to route the claims correctly to the insurance payer. Finding errors before submitting claims.
answersDetail.7. If a batch is missing, what should we: If batch is missing we check the encounter; if encounter is found we need to get confirmation from the client.
answersDetail.8. If Payer ID is Missing, what will hap: If a payer ID is missing we check all possible ways to find it; if still not found we check the clearinghouse.
answersDetail.9. What is rejection and type of rejecti: Claims get rejected due to errors or missing information. Types: 1. Clearing house Rejection 2. Insurance Rejection
answersDetail.10. Why insurance requesting medical rec: If the claim needs additional supporting documents to issue payment, insurance requests medical records to reprocess the claim.
answersDetail.11. Why we are adding modifier 25 for E&: When other procedures are billed with E&M services we need to add 25 Modifier to specify the services provided by the provider.
answersDetail.13. Why we are doing Print HCFA?: If electronic or online payer portal submission is not supported, we need to do print HCFA which is a paper claim form.
answersDetail.14. Which task should we prioritize firs: Faxing. Reason: Print HCFA takes more time which results in delayed payment.
answersDetail.15. Why claim submission is important?: If we do not submit the claim, there is no payment which results in revenue loss — we may lose the client.
